instructions: This conversation is fictional. Listen to the conversation before reading the transcript and answer independently. After submitting, check the transcript and reasons for any errors.
transcript:
Mina: We have ten people for the Sunday walk. Can someone check the trail before we invite everyone to the meeting point?
Noah: I asked the park guide this morning. She said the path beside the lake is open, but the old bridge is closed. We should not guess our way around it.
Mina: Then let us meet outside the station at ten, not nine. Is there a landmark that everyone can recognize?
Noah: Yes, there is a blue clock at the first junction. Walk along the sidewalk toward it. The pavement for cars is on the other side of the fence, so the group should stay together.
Mina: What happens at the intersection near the clock?
Noah: We turn east and follow the wide path to the stream. There is a small shelter beside the water. The notice says it is a good place for our first short stop.
Mina: I have a compass. Does the route go south after that?
Noah: No. We go west through a meadow and then pass a field. We do not go beyond the gate into the farm. The farmer has asked visitors to use the marked trail instead.
Mina: The map shows a hill. Do we have to climb it?
Noah: No. The upper slope is steep, and the narrow track there is muddy. Our guide chooses a gentler way through the valley. At the end, we descend a short path toward the visitor center.
Mina: I also see a tunnel on the map. Is that part of the walk?
Noah: It is not. We will read the updated notice again before Sunday. If anyone needs help or loses sight of the group, they can call the guide using the number on the note.
Mina: Good. I will write both the ten o'clock meeting time and the guide's number. That should make the plan easier to understand.
